RAG Reranking with LangChain - Building Smarter Retrieval Pipelines
Let’s be honest. Just tossing a user’s query into a retrieval system and passing the top few documents to a language model isn’t always enough. Heck, sometimes it’s flat-out wrong. That’s where reranking enters the scene like a hero with a magnifying glass - scrutinizing document relevance and surfacing the best picks for generation.
No fluff. Just real, messy, powerful steps.
🌱 What Even Is RAG Reranking?
RAG stands for Retrieval-Augmented Generation. The idea? A large language model (LLM) doesn’t operate in isolation. It brings in extra brainpower 🚀👇
•
Step 1: You ask a question.
•
Step 2: A retriever scans a massive sea of documents. It grabs the top few nuggets.
•
Step 3: Those get passed to an LLM. The LLM uses them to generate a final response.
Neat in theory, but here’s the catch.
Top-5 isn’t always Top-Smart. Some retrieved docs are… bland. Even irrelevant. Imagine asking about RAG reranking and getting a paragraph about raccoons. Close in letters, far in meaning.
That’s why we rerank.
Reranking takes that list and reshuffles it. Prioritizes quality. Instead of trusting the retriever blindly, you give the model a second voice - a smarter voice - to re-judge the results.
Cross-encoders, small LLMs, expert scorers - all rerankers. They grade the response candidates, one by one. Survivors get passed on.
Let’s go build this system.
🧰 What You’ll Need
Before we start, make sure these packages are installed:
•
langchain
•
langchain-community
•
langchain-openai
•
faiss-cpu (vector similarity FTW)
Here’s the one-liner to install all of them:
pip install langchain langchain-community langchain-openai faiss-cpu
All set? Let’s build it better.
🔧 1. Build the Vectorstore - Brains in a Box
LangChain uses vector databases to store transformed (embedded) documents. Think of it like converting sentences into mathematical clouds. You can search through these clouds insanely fast.
Here’s how we start:
from langchain_community.embeddings import OpenAIEmbeddings from langchain_community.vectorstores import FAISS # Sample data - pretend this is richer than it is documents = [ "LangChain is a framework for developing LLM-powered apps.", "RAG reranking improves relevance.", "Vector search is essential for LLM pipelines." ] # Initialize embedding model embeddings = OpenAIEmbeddings() # Drop them into FAISS db = FAISS.from_texts(documents, embedding=embeddings)
Your vectorstore now holds the “thoughts” of each document. Embedding converts them into vectors. FAISS stores them efficiently.
Next: we retrieve.
📥 2. Make a Retriever
Let’s ask FAISS to behave like a student who always picks five answers, even when unsure.
retriever = db.as_retriever(search_kwargs={"k": 5})
Keep this in mind: retrievers are fast. But they’re shallow. They check for surface similarity, not deep meaning. Which is fine… until you want real results.
So we fix that.
💡 3. Plug in the Reranker - The Refiner
Bad inputs = bad outputs. Better inputs = better LLM performance.
You want your documents reranked before being stuffed into a prompt. Here’s how we use a language model to do it:
from langchain_core.rerankers import LLMReranker from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI # The reranker uses a small LLM - not the full GPT-4, but smart enough llm = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-3.5-turbo") reranker = LLMReranker.from_llm(llm=llm)
This LLM will get descriptions of each document and judge how relevant they are to the question, filtering irrelevant ones.
Think of it as your retriever’s editor.
🔄 4. Build the RAG Chain
LangChain has this beautiful feature: the pipe | operator. It chains components together. Think Unix pipes. But for AI.
Let’s stack our components like bricks:
from langchain_core.runnables import RunnablePassthrough from langchain_core.prompts import ChatPromptTemplate from langchain_core.output_parsers import StrOutputParser # Our prompt prompt = ChatPromptTemplate.from_template(""" You are a helpful assistant. Use the following context to answer the question. Context: {context} Question: {question} """) # Chain it all up rag_chain = ( {"question": RunnablePassthrough()} | { "question": lambda d: d["question"], "context": retriever | reranker } | prompt | llm | StrOutputParser() )
What’s happening here?
•
Input flows in as {“question”: value}
•
Passthrough keeps the question intact
•
Retriever grabs raw context
•
Reranker refines it
•
Prompt wraps up the question + context
•
LLM writes the response
•
StrOutputParser extracts the text
🚀 5. Run It!
Now for the test. Hit it with a question:
question = "What is RAG reranking?" response = rag_chain.invoke(question) print(response)
You should see a response that’s lifted by reranking. More relevant. Less fluff. Sharper. LLMs make better predictions when fed clean, semantically rich input. That’s the trick.
🎯 Why Rerank at All?
Because garbage in = garbage out.
Plain retrievers operate on similarity, not meaning. They miss context. They get fooled by keywords. Reranking adds intention. It asks, “What is this question really about?” and finds docs fit to answer.
Here’s what you really get:
•
90% noise → 10% gold becomes → 90% gold 💥
•
Cuts hallucination by cleaning context upfront
•
Improves answer accuracy without touching the LLM itself
•
Easy to scale - plug into thousands of docs, rerank, done
In short, reranking takes “meh” and makes it “whoa.”
🧪 Wrapping Up
We keep asking models to be smarter, more helpful, more right. But what if the real solution isn’t inside the model - it’s before it?
That’s what reranking is. It’s the part we kept skipping because our search felt “good enough.” Not anymore.
With LangChain’s new pipe-based chaining and reranker support, there’s no excuse not to build in quality control. One tiny reranker = massive uplift in results.
So next time you fire up your RAG pipeline… add that middle layer. Add the reranker. Watch your smart become smarter.
Stay sharp. Keep tinkering. The future is in the details.
